---
title: "Criterion-specific excess risk of a common report"
subtitle: "4.5 · commonality costs from postrank, with live and archived examples"
description: "Increase in each criterion's risk relative to its own optimum in the same report family."
---

Under a common report, a criterion can carry higher risk than under grades chosen for that criterion alone. The gap $\Delta_k$ is its commonality cost within the same report family and withholding price.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** Excess risks are .0490 on score A and .0145 on score B, joining each criterion's own minimum to its common-report risk.
- **Score A only.** The common report matches score A's own optimum: score A gives up 0 and score B gives up .148.
- **w .70.** The common report becomes {A} > {B, C, D} > {E, F}, with excess risks .0253 on score A and .0563 on score B.
- **Score B only.** Two common reports tie: score A pays .158 under one and .170 under the other, while score B pays 0.
- **Thirty sites, higher price.** The archived common report states 276 pairs; snap's cost is .446 and its wrong share among stated pairs is .784.
- **Thirty sites, lower price.** The common report withholds every pair, yet separate optima give costs .0895, .0749, and .102 for poverty, frl, and snap.

<details>
<summary>Scope and archived bounds</summary>

The package writes this risk difference as $\Delta_k$. It measures the cost of a common report under the chosen loss; judging the weights or downstream consequences requires additional information. The thirty-site results come from archived posterior-draw analyses whose intervals bound the solver search minimum.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
cc <- postrank_commonality_cost(postrank(pr_tutorial$two, weights=c(score_A=.5,score_B=.5), tau=.2, G_max=3, backend="highs", report_card=FALSE, fragility=FALSE), backend="highs")
cc$table[, c("criterion_id", "cost_lower", "cost_upper")]
```
:::
